purpose: Test whether prior history is itself a hidden dependency carrier across otherwise different JSON domains.

observed_operator: predictable choices measurable from prior history
future target conditional on complete PRE_RETURN view
previous evidence changes whether live step is justified
each live experiment should reduce necessity of the next
impact states preserve historical decision path
past crisis changes next search state
old model is retained as failure context
next action is bounded by prior discernment
witness points onward without becoming source
prior witness changes the social state of information

cross_domain_findings.name: HISTORY_IS_A_DECISION_INPUT
cross_domain_findings.pattern: PAST OBSERVATION -> CURRENT INFORMATION SET -> NEXT ALLOWED ACTION

cross_domain_findings.name: HISTORY_CARRIER_CAN_REPLACE_SHARED_HARDWARE
cross_domain_findings.pattern: A -> RECORDED_HISTORY -> B creates dependency even when A and B use different infrastructure

real.basis: Explicit history-wise dependence is stated in sequential, anytime-valid and causal-consistency witnesses.

blind.basis: The operator survives removal of filenames, titles, authors and lineage labels.

rewiring_rule: Preserve witness count, field counts, schema and marginal distributions while permuting only prior-history links between earlier and later observations.
null_rule: Schema-matched relation permutation destroying chronological dependency while preserving record-level statistics.
claim_ceiling: This scan establishes a cross-domain structural recurrence candidate, not causal proof and not machine novelty.
